text: Le match Kingsmoor FC contre Westport Albion s'est terminé sur un score de 3-3, avec beaucoup d'actions et de retournements. Viktor Quinlan a brillé en marquant deux buts, dont un penalty, et a parcouru près de 11 km, preuve de son énorme forme, il a même été élu meilleur joueur avec une note de 9.9[#152][#222]. Kingsmoor FC a dominé la possession et a eu de belles opportunités grâce à un jeu large et des centres. Westport Albion a tiré plus souvent (18 tirs contre 10) et a aussi marqué 3 fois, grâce à leur jeu direct et vertical[#401][#553]. Le tournant est arrivé à la 81e minute avec un carton rouge pour Felix Barros, avant que Kingsmoor FC n'égalise très vite par Luca Iversen, aidé par Mason Morales[#1494][#1516]. Les changements tactiques ont rendu ce match encore plus intense, avec Kingsmoor FC qui a pressé plus haut en fin de match et Westport qui a tenté de ralentir pour tenir le score[#1187][#1459].

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for fan audience in fr

- Viktor Quinlan scored 2 goals with a combined xG of 1.051 and was named player of the match with a rating of 9.9 and 10.97 km covered [#152, #222].
- Westport Albion had higher total shots (18) and shots on target (11) compared to Kingsmoor FC (10 shots, 3 on target) but both ended with 3 goals each [team_stats].
- The match featured tactical changes with Kingsmoor FC increasing press and directness from 65' to chase the game, and Westport Albion dropping deeper and lowering tempo from 79' to protect their lead [#1187, #1459].
- A red card was issued to Felix Barros (Kingsmoor FC) at 81', impacting the match just before the equalizer at 82' by Luca Iversen (xG 0.888) assisted by Mason Morales [#1494, #1516].
- Westport Albion had a higher xG of 3.96 than Kingsmoor FC's 3.45 overall, indicating slightly better quality chances overall despite the 3-3 draw [team_stats].

- Kingsmoor FC's first goal was a penalty scored by Viktor Quinlan early in the match, stemming directly from a set piece (penalty spot), reflecting a clinical finishing ability rather than open play combination [#152].  
- The second Kingsmoor FC goal involved a sustained buildup from a ball regain, with 8 passes over 26 seconds involving multiple players, demonstrating their 4-4-2 formation's focus on wide and crossing play through patient possession and build-up from the back, culminating in a medium assist by Felix Duarte to Quinlan [#222].  
- Westport Albion's equalizing goals came from more direct and vertical play, consistent with their style and 4-4-2 formation: one goal resulted from a short assist by Kian Castillo after a 7-pass 25-second buildup from regain, and another goal featured a cross from Dylan Rahman after a 10-pass sequence lasting nearly 40 seconds emphasizing vertical progression and crossing [#401, #553].  
- Kingsmoor FC's tactical change at 65 minutes to press higher and play more direct indicates an adjustment to regain momentum while chasing the game, increasing pressing intensity (press parameter 0.68) and line height (0.62) to force turnovers higher up, matching their wide and crossing style to create quick attacking chances in Westport’s half [#1187].  
- In contrast, Westport Albion’s subsequent tactical shift at 79 minutes to drop deeper and slow tempo (press and line height dropped to 0.25, tempo 0.35) aimed to protect their lead by reducing pressing aggression and field tilt, focusing on defensive solidity rather than facilitating quick attacking transitions in line with their direct style [#1459].  
- The late Kingsmoor FC equalizer at 82 minutes came shortly after a second yellow red card to Westport’s Felix Barros, with a quick buildup of just 2 passes over 8.5 seconds starting from a regain, finished by a cross from Mason Morales to Luca Iversen, showing Kingsmoor’s continued reliance on crossing from wide areas to exploit the numerical advantage and break Westport's now defensive setup [#1516].
